plugin.name: Player CLI
plugin.settings.title: Player CLI
plugin.settings.binary-path.label: Path to the player-cli binary (blank = use PATH). Only used to start the background player when it isn't already running — everything else talks to it directly over its socket.
actions.play-toggle.name: Play/Stop Track
actions.play-toggle.target.label: Target
actions.play-toggle.library.label: Pick from library
actions.play-toggle.library.subtitle: Audio files found under your configured library directories (see `player-cli library add`)
actions.play-toggle.library.empty: No library configured — see `player-cli library add`
actions.play-toggle.path.label: Audio file path or filename (or pick one above)
actions.play-toggle.uri.label: Spotify URI, share link, or <kind>:<id>, e.g. spotify:playlist:37i9dQZF1DXcBWIGoYBM5M
actions.play-toggle.replace.label: Replace
actions.play-toggle.replace.subtitle: Stop every other track before playing this one
actions.play-toggle.loop.label: Loop
actions.play-toggle.loop.subtitle: Restart from the beginning when it finishes, until stopped. Only applies the next time this starts the track.
actions.play-toggle.fade.label: Fade (ms)
actions.play-toggle.fade.subtitle: Ramp this track's volume over this many milliseconds instead of changing it instantly - when this key starts/stops it, and when it's paused/resumed elsewhere (e.g. via Pause/Resume All). 0 disables fading. Only applies the next time this starts the track.
actions.stop-all.name: Stop All Tracks
actions.stop-all.label: Stop All
actions.pause-resume-all.name: Pause/Resume All
actions.pause-resume-all.target.label: Target
actions.pause-resume-all.action.label: Command
actions.pause-resume-all.action.subtitle: Sent via `player-cli spotify` (playerctl) over MPRIS - no Spotify Web API needed
actions.adjust-volume.name: Adjust Volume
actions.adjust-volume.target.label: Target
actions.adjust-volume.step.label: Step
actions.adjust-volume.step.subtitle: Percent per key press (negative to decrease). On a dial, only the magnitude is used - turning clockwise always raises volume, counter-clockwise always lowers it; pressing the dial still applies this value as-is.
